title: Program.cs, Middleware Pipeline, and appsettings.json
description: Understand the Program.cs entry point, how the middleware pipeline processes HTTP requests, and how appsettings.json stores application configuration.

terms.definition: The entry point of an ASP.NET Core application where services are registered and the middleware pipeline is built.
Software components assembled into a pipeline that handles HTTP requests and responses.
A JSON configuration file in the project root that stores key-value settings like connection strings and feature flags.
The top-level object created by WebApplication.CreateBuilder that exposes both the service container and the HTTP pipeline.
A service injected into components to determine the current hosting environment (Development, Staging, or Production).

data.text: ASP.NET Core applications are configured across three main files: the **.csproj project file**, **Program.cs**, and **appsettings.json**. Together they define how your app is built, which services it uses, and how it responds to HTTP requests.

The `.csproj` file is an XML file that defines your project's SDK, target framework, and NuGet package dependencies. Visual Studio hides this file by default — right-click the project in Solution Explorer and choose **Edit Project File** to open it.

data.text: Program.cs is where everything comes together. It has two phases: first you **register services** on the DI container, then you **build the middleware pipeline** that handles HTTP requests.

data.title: Top-to-bottom, inside-out
data.text: Read Program.cs top-to-bottom: registrations happen first (before Build()), middleware is added after (after Build()). The order of UseXxx() calls matters — it is the exact order requests pass through the pipeline.
